Forwarding HealthSync's redlines and Evelyn's note. Quick commercial summary for context:
- Pilot starts Dec 1 if contracts in place.
- Contract value for initial 6 months ~ $120k (pilot + onboarding).
- Procurement needs DPA + SCCs in place to push to signature.

Key commercial asks from my side:
- We should avoid open-ended acceptance of any subprocessor additions. Recommend we counter with 30 days' notice (not 14) and allow "object and audit" rights limited to data types and where strictly necessary.
- Confirm whether the Order Form needs an explicit Data Processing Schedule reference (prefer to link the DPA in the Order Form to avoid duplicate clauses).

Priyom / Marcus — can you take the lead on a redline that:
1) Accepts SCC framework but maps roles where Redwood is "importer";
2) Adds a 30-day subprocessor notification and a simple objection path;
3) Adds a TIA appendix placeholder and commits to provide hosting locations and a subprocessor list within 5 business days of countersignature.

I've attached a commercial-friendly redline draft: redwood_proposed_dpa_redlines.docx.

Thanks — LMK if you'd like me to join the call with HealthSync.
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: MSA and Order Form - DPA redlines (HealthSync)

Team — reviewed HealthSync's redlines and Laura's commercial note. Attached: redwood_dpa_markedup.docx (key snippets below). I recommend the following position to preserve product flexibility while being reasonable for the pilot: 

1) SCCs and role mapping
- We can accept the EU SCCs as "Importer" only if HealthSync remains the Exporter. We should not accept language that flips responsibilities entirely onto Redwood for transfers initiated by the customer. Proposed snippet: Redwood will act as "data importer" under the SCCs, processing on behalf of the data exporter, and will implement technical and organisational measures described in the DPA.

2) Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA)
- Agree to include a TIA appendix but limit the scope: Redwood will provide a description of transfer destinations and supplementary safeguards. HealthSync remains responsible for customer-side risk evaluations and instructions. We can commit to producing a basic TIA within 5 business days of countersignature; complex jurisdictional assessments will require legal retainer / additional scope.

3) Subprocessors and notice period
- Counter to 30 days notice (commercial wants 30) but allow accelerated notice for security-critical subprocessors. Include a clause for an objection right limited to material data protection risks, with a reasonable cure period (15 business days).

4) Order Form linkage and deletion/return
- Make DPA the authoritative data processing schedule referenced in the Order Form. Add explicit deletion/return timeline (30 days after termination for pilot data, longer for retention mandated by law).

Next steps I propose:
- Send redlined DPA back to HealthSync with comments and proposed DocuSign flow.
- Offer a technical/legal sync on 2026-11-08 or 2026-11-09 (30 min) to resolve remaining TIA items.

I attach the redline document and a short set of suggested language snippets for each of the items above. If HealthSync pushes a narrower SCC role mapping or unilateral responsibility for TIAs, we should escalate to procurement/legal for commercial pushback.

— Priyom
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
